findings.problem: TODO comment cargo-cults Rayon for a 4-byte fixed-size input. Rayon task creation and scheduling overhead vastly exceeds any benefit for 4 elements.
findings.failure_mode: Degraded performance: thread-pool overhead dominates computation time, making the function 10-100x slower than the sequential version on a 4-element input.
findings.fix: Remove the Rayon TODO. For 4 elements, sequential iteration is optimal. Do not use Rayon without measured scaling evidence on large pure transforms.

findings.problem: TODO comment references SmallVec for a function that always returns exactly 4 elements. SmallVec is only appropriate when the small-size distribution is known and measured.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary dependency and code complexity for a fixed-size 4-element output where the caller knows the exact size. SmallVec adds no benefit with a deterministic size of 4.
findings.fix: Remove the SmallVec TODO. If heap allocation must stay, keep Vec. If the caller owns the buffer, pass an output slice or SmallVec<[&str; 4]> only after measuring.

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<&'static str> for a pure deterministic transformation of 4 bytes. Always allocates a heap Vec even for the known size of 4.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every call. For a hot encoder/parser path this compounds allocation pressure.
findings.fix: Return a fixed-size array [&'static str; 4] or accept a caller-owned output buffer. Pure deterministic functions on fixed-size inputs should avoid heap allocations.
